Whether it becomes a convention is a separate judgement — a CV photo is arguably a layout matter, and the same page's treatment of anonymised CVs turns on gender and origin, so an entry built here risks the protected-trait constraint. Flagging rather than prescribing.

## Important and missing

1. **Blue Card lower salary threshold.** § 18g(1) sentence 2 (verified today) sets a reduced threshold for named ISCO occupation groups — which include ICT and engineering families — and for anyone whose degree is recent. Entry 3 says "a threshold", singular. A candidate below the general figure may wrongly conclude they are ineligible when they sit in a shortage group. Highest-value gap in the set.
2. **Job change while holding a Blue Card.** § 18g(4) (verified today): no immigration-authority permission is needed for a job change, but during the first months of employment the authority may suspend and refuse it. This table's user is by definition someone applying to a new employer; a Blue Card holder applying out of their current job has a hard constraint here and nothing in the entry mentions it.
3. **KSchG small-business exclusion (§ 23).** Covered above under entry 5; listing separately because it also changes how a candidate should price probation and notice terms at a small employer.
4. **§ 81a is not universally available** — restricted to the residence purposes the provision enumerates, and it is initiated by agreement between employer and authority, so an employer with no such Vereinbarung cannot simply opt in late. Entry 3 reads as if the route is always on the table.
5. **The Anschreiben's status at international employers.** The entry flags this honestly in `unverified` item 3 and then writes the convention as though the letter is universally screened. Since large international tech employers in Germany routinely run CV-only ATS flows, the gap between "the federal agency treats it as standard" and "this employer wants one" is the operative question — and `applies_when` already half-concedes it ("not routed through an employer portal which explicitly asks for a CV only"). Either source the practice or move the strength of the claim into `applies_when`.

entry.application_artifacts:
US AND UK — WHAT A COMPLETE APPLICATION CONTAINS BEYOND A CV

US, private sector (PARTLY UNVERIFIED). The verified, sourced component is the employer's own online application form, which sits alongside whatever CV you upload and carries screening questions the posting does not show. The U.S. Department of Justice's IER FAQ confirms the two that matter: "Generally, an employer may ask job applicants if they have the legal right to work in the United States and if they will need sponsorship for an employment visa" (justice.gov/crt/iers-frequently-asked-questions-faqs, retrieved 2026-08-09). Treat the form itself — not the CV — as the artifact that gates you. Whether a cover letter is expected, and whether portfolios/GitHub links are read, I COULD NOT SOURCE; see the unverified section.

US, after an offer. Form I-9 is completed on hire. IER states: "The Department of Homeland Security has designated several combinations of acceptable documents from which workers can choose to prove their identity and permission to work... A worker is allowed to produce either List A documentation (establishing both identity and permission to work), or a combination of documentation from List B (establishing identity) and List C (establishing permission to work). Employers can't specify which documents they [require]." MUST NOT: let a recruiter narrow you to one named document — IER calls that an unfair documentary practice (same URL, retrieved 2026-08-09).

UK, Civil Service. The artifact is written evidence against the specific Success Profile elements the job description names — not a general cover letter. Cabinet Office, "Success Profiles" (gov.uk/government/publications/success-profiles, retrieved 2026-08-09): "A Success Profile is made up of 5 elements: behaviours... strengths... ability... experience... technical... Not all of the elements are relevant to every role." The companion page "Success Profiles: Civil Service behaviours" (retrieved 2026-08-09) adds: "recruiting managers will choose a selection of behaviours which are best suited to the specific job role. You will not be asked to demonstrate all Civil Service Behaviours for one role," that behaviours "are specific to the grade level of the job role," that assessment may be by "application form requiring written examples," and: "In your own examples, consider using the STAR method which allows you to set the scene, show what and how you did and the overall outcome."

UK, NHS. The artifact is the NHS Jobs application form with its supporting-information / supporting-evidence sections, written against the person specification. NHS Jobs, "Making successful applications" (jobs.nhs.uk/candidate/search/advice/making-successful-applications, retrieved 2026-08-09): "All employers will be judging how well your application matches the 'person specification'... The applicants who closely match the person specification will be the ones that are shortlisted for interview," and "Never submit the same application form twice. Always adapt it to show how you meet the person specification of the particular post you are applying for," and "The 'personal information' and 'monitoring information' sections will not be used for shortlisting."

UK NHS — WHAT IT MUST NOT CONTAIN. Evidence is entered criterion by criterion in separate boxes, and those boxes must be anonymous. NHSBSA, "How to apply for a job in NHS Jobs user guide – Add your supporting evidence" (nhsbsa.nhs.uk/sites/default/files/2022-05/How%20to%20apply%20for%20a%20job%20in%20NHS%20Jobs%20-%20Add%20your%20supporting%20evidence.pdf, retrieved 2026-08-09): "Important: Do not include personal information that could be used to identify you such as your name or contact details." The same guide notes "'Qualifications' and 'Experience' are mandatory essential criteria" with further criteria added by the employer, and that a character limit is shown on the form. A supporting statement written as a signed narrative letter breaks this rule.

UK, both public-sector routes, before you apply. Where sponsorship is in question the register of licensed sponsors is a document you consult, not one you submit: UK Visas and Immigration, "Register of licensed sponsors: workers" (gov.uk/government/publications/register-of-licensed-sponsors-workers, retrieved 2026-08-09) — "List of organisations licensed to sponsor workers on the Worker and Temporary Worker immigration routes... It includes information about the category of workers they're licensed to sponsor and their sponsorship rating."

conventions.text_en: US application forms ask whether you are legally allowed to work in the United States and whether you will need visa sponsorship as separate questions, and the Department of Justice confirms an employer may ask both. Whether the employer sponsors at all is normally a policy fixed before the role was ever advertised, so this filter can run before anyone reads your experience. Answer each question on its own terms instead of collapsing them into one, and find out the employer's sponsorship posture before you invest in the application. One limit worth knowing: an employer may restrict hiring to US citizens only where a law, regulation, executive order or government contract requires it, and the Immigrant and Employee Rights Section takes complaints where that is not the case.
conventions.text_zh: 美国的申请表会把「你现在是否已获准在美国合法工作」和「你是否需要签证担保」拆成互相独立的问题，美国司法部确认雇主有权同时问这两项。公司是否提供担保通常在职位发布之前就已定为政策，因此这道筛选可能在任何人看你的履历之前就自动执行。请把两个问题分开如实回答，不要合并处理；在投入精力之前先弄清这家雇主对担保的立场。另有一条界限值得知道：只有在法律、法规、行政命令或政府合同要求的情况下，雇主才可以把招聘限定为美国公民；不属于这些情形的「仅限美国公民」，司法部 Immigrant and Employee Rights Section 是受理投诉的。
conventions.applies_when: Applying to a US employer through its own application form or job portal.
conventions.source_detail: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division — "IER's Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)", https://www.justice.gov/crt/iers-frequently-asked-questions-faqs, retrieved 2026-08-09. Verbatim: "Generally, an employer may ask job applicants if they have the legal right to work in the United States and if they will need sponsorship for an employment visa." and "An employer may restrict hiring to U.S. citizens only when a law, regulation, executive order, or government contract requires the employer to do so."
conventions.why: The posting almost never states the employer's sponsorship policy. The questions surface only after you open the form, and the knockout is silent — you get a rejection, not an explanation.

conventions.text_en: Some US employers sit in a statutory class that is exempt from the H-1B numerical cap: institutions of higher education, nonprofit entities related to or affiliated with them, nonprofit research organisations, and governmental research organisations. Postings never mention this, yet it changes what the employer can do and when, because a cap-exempt petition does not depend on the annual registration cycle. The regulation also lets work for another employer count as cap-exempt where the person spends at least a minimum share of work time — the figure is set in the rule — on duties that further the qualifying institution's mission, and it says that work performed 'at' the institution can include remote and off-site work. So the question that actually predicts what is possible is what kind of organisation the employer is, not whether the advert says sponsorship is available.
conventions.text_zh: 有一类美国雇主在法规上不受 H-1B 名额上限限制：高等教育机构、与其存在关联或附属关系的非营利实体、非营利研究机构，以及政府研究机构。招聘启事从不提这一点，但它直接决定雇主能做什么、什么时候能做，因为「免名额」申请不依赖每年一次的抽签登记周期。法规还规定：即使不是由上述机构直接雇用，只要本人把不低于法规所定比例的工作时间用于服务该合格机构使命的职务，也可算作免名额，并且法规明确「在」该机构完成的工作可以包括远程和异地工作。所以真正能预测可行性的问题，是这家雇主属于哪一类组织，而不是启事上有没有写「提供签证担保」。
conventions.applies_when: Considering US employers where an H-1B petition might eventually be needed, especially universities, hospitals, research institutes and their affiliated nonprofits.
conventions.source_detail: eCFR, 8 CFR 214.2(h)(8)(iii)(F) — "Cap exemptions under sections 214(g)(5)(A) and (B) of the Act". Text verified from the eCFR bulk XML endpoint https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-08-01/title-8.xml?part=214&section=214.2 (HTTP 200, retrieved 2026-08-09); human-readable section at https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/section-214.2 (HTTP 200, retrieved 2026-08-09). Verbatim includes: "An alien is not subject to the numerical limitations identified in section 214(g)(1)(A) of the Act if the alien qualifies for an exemption under section 214(g)(5) of the Act"; the affiliation tests at (F)(2); and "Work performed 'at' the qualifying institution may include work performed in the United States through telework, remote work, or other off-site work."
conventions.why: Cap-exempt status is a property of the employing organisation, not of the vacancy, so it is invisible in the advert. Candidates screen adverts for the phrase 'sponsorship available' and skip entire categories of employer for whom the annual cap is simply not a constraint.

conventions.text_en: The STEM extension of Optional Practical Training imposes conditions on the employer, not only on the student. The regulation requires that the employer be enrolled in E-Verify and remain a participant in good standing, that it hold a tax identification number, and that it sign the Training Plan for STEM OPT Students (Form I-983) and accept the reporting duties that come with it. A willing employer that is not enrolled in E-Verify cannot host this arrangement no matter how much it wants to. Adverts never disclose E-Verify enrolment, so raise it with the recruiter early rather than discovering it at the offer stage.
conventions.text_zh: OPT 的 STEM 延期把条件加在雇主身上，而不只是学生身上。法规要求雇主已注册 E-Verify 并持续保持良好参与状态、拥有税务识别号，并签署《STEM OPT 学生培训计划》（Form I-983）以及承担随之而来的报告义务。一个再愿意配合的雇主，只要没有注册 E-Verify，就无法支持这一安排。招聘启事从不披露是否注册了 E-Verify，所以要在流程早期就向招聘方问清楚，而不是等到发 offer 时才发现。
conventions.applies_when: Any US role where an OPT STEM extension is or may become part of the plan, particularly at small employers and startups.
conventions.source_detail: eCFR, 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C)(5) "Employer qualification" and (C)(6) "Employer reporting". Text verified from https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-08-01/title-8.xml?part=214&section=214.2 (HTTP 200, retrieved 2026-08-09); human-readable section at https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/section-214.2 (HTTP 200, retrieved 2026-08-09). Verbatim: "The student's employer is enrolled in E-Verify... and the employer remains a participant in good standing with E-Verify, as determined by USCIS. An employer must also have an employer identification number (EIN) used for tax purposes." and "...unless the employer agrees, by signing the Training Plan for STEM OPT Students, Form I-983 or successor form, to report..."
conventions.why: Candidates research their own eligibility and assume employer cooperation is just goodwill. The blocking condition is an administrative enrolment the employer either has or does not have, and it is never stated in a posting.

conventions.text_en: US employment is at-will by default: either side may end it at any time and, unless the parties agreed otherwise, neither owes the other notice. The customary short resignation notice is a norm, not an entitlement. That shapes hiring in ways the posting never states — US employers commonly expect a near-term start date and read a long notice period as a scheduling problem, while the at-will wording in a US offer letter is standard boilerplate rather than a warning sign. The UK is the mirror image: statutory minimum notice applies once you have been in a job beyond a short qualifying period, your contract can require longer, and gov.uk warns you may be in breach of contract if you do not give enough notice. A UK start date is therefore negotiated around a notice period as a matter of course. Applying into both markets without adjusting the availability you state will burn you in one direction or the other.
conventions.text_zh: 美国的雇佣默认是「随意雇佣」（at-will）：除非双方另有约定，任何一方都可以随时终止，且互不负提前通知义务。惯例上的短期离职通知是习惯，不是法定权利。这会以启事上从不写明的方式影响招聘——美国雇主通常期待较近的到岗日期，会把很长的通知期视为排期问题；而 offer letter 里的 at-will 条款属于标准套话，不是危险信号。英国正好相反：在职超过一段较短的资格期后即适用法定最短通知期，合同还可以约定更长，gov.uk 明确提醒通知不足可能构成违约。因此英国的到岗日期天然是围绕通知期谈的。同时投这两个市场却不调整你所声明的可到岗时间，必然会在其中一边吃亏。
conventions.applies_when: Any application into both markets, and any moment you state your availability or read an offer letter.
conventions.source_detail: US: State of California, Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Labor Standards Enforcement — "Termination of Employment" (Rev. 1/2011), https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/TerminationOfEmployment.pdf, retrieved 2026-08-09. Verbatim: "Within the State of California, employment may be terminated at the will of either party. Both the employer and the employee are free to end the employment relationship at any time, with no penalty being assessed to either. Unless the parties have previously agreed to the contrary, there is no notice required to be given by either party." (At-will is state law and this is one state's official statement of the doctrine, not a nationwide statute.) UK: GOV.UK — "Handing in your notice: Giving notice", https://www.gov.uk/handing-in-your-notice/giving-notice, retrieved 2026-08-09, which states a statutory minimum notice obligation after a short period in the job and: "You may be in breach of your contract if you do not give enough notice."
conventions.why: Both defaults are so ordinary inside their own market that no one writes them down. A candidate carrying UK notice-period assumptions into a US process looks slow and hesitant; a candidate carrying US at-will assumptions into a UK process promises a start date they cannot legally deliver.

conventions.text_en: Whether a US posting shows a pay range is mostly a question of which state's law reaches the role, not of how open the employer is. Colorado requires employers to disclose compensation in all job postings and notices, internal and public, and that disclosure must include information about benefits and how and when to apply. New York requires a compensation range for advertised job, promotion and transfer opportunities at employers above a size threshold set in the statute, requires employers to state clearly if a position is commission-based, and forbids retaliation against people who ask about it. So read a published range as a legally required disclosure of a band, not as an offer or a sign of generosity; read its absence as a fact about jurisdiction rather than about the employer. Where the law does apply, a missing range is a compliance failure and both states run complaint channels.
conventions.text_zh: 美国的招聘启事上有没有薪酬区间，主要取决于该职位受哪个州的法律管辖，而不是雇主开不开放。科罗拉多州要求雇主在所有对内和对外的职位发布与通知中披露薪酬，且披露内容必须包括福利信息以及如何、何时申请。纽约州要求达到法定规模门槛的雇主在所有对外发布的职位、晋升和调岗机会中列出薪酬区间，明确标注是否为提成制，并禁止对询问此事的人进行报复。因此，看到区间时把它当作法律要求披露的一个「带宽」，而不是报价或雇主慷慨的信号；看不到区间时，把它理解为管辖权的事实，而不是雇主的态度。在法律确实适用的地方，缺少区间属于违规，这两个州都设有投诉渠道。
conventions.applies_when: Reading US postings, comparing employers, or preparing to discuss compensation in a US process.
conventions.source_detail: Colorado Department of Labor and Employment — "Equal Pay for Equal Work Act", https://cdle.colorado.gov/equalpaytransparency, retrieved 2026-08-09. Verbatim: "Part 2, referred to by the Division as 'Pay Transparency,' requires transparency in pay and job opportunities. Specifically, it requires employers to disclose compensation in all job postings and notices, both internal and public. This disclosure must include information about benefits and how and when to apply." New York State Department of Labor — "Pay Transparency", https://dol.ny.gov/pay-transparency, retrieved 2026-08-09. Verbatim: "Labor Law Section 194-B requires New York State businesses with four or more employees to provide job descriptions and list compensation ranges for designated job opportunities, promotions, and transfers... Employers must also clearly state if a position is commission-based. Finally, this new law prohibits employers from retaliating against employees or applicants who request this information." Colorado and New York are the two states verified here; other states also have such laws but I did not fetch their official pages, so they are not named.
conventions.why: Candidates infer employer character from whether a range is shown, and treat the top of a posted range as a target. Both inferences are wrong: the range exists because a statute compels it in that jurisdiction, and it describes a band the employer believes accurate at posting time.

conventions.text_en: Once you are hired in the US you complete Form I-9, and the choice of documents is yours. The government has designated combinations from which workers choose: either a document that establishes both identity and permission to work, or a combination drawn from the identity list and the permission-to-work list. Employers of any size are barred from unfair documentary practices — requesting more or different documents than are required, rejecting documents that reasonably appear genuine, or specifying certain documents over others. None of this appears in a posting, and a recruiter or onboarding team demanding one named document is exactly the situation the Immigrant and Employee Rights Section takes complaints about.
conventions.text_zh: 在美国被录用后要填写 Form I-9，而选哪些证件是你的权利。官方规定了可选的证件组合：既可以出示一份同时证明身份和工作许可的证件，也可以从「身份」清单和「工作许可」清单中各取其一组合使用。任何规模的雇主都不得从事「不当证件要求」——即索取超出规定数量或种类的证件、拒收看起来合理真实的证件，或指定必须使用某些特定证件。这些内容不会出现在招聘启事里；招聘人员或入职团队点名要求某一份特定证件，正是司法部 Immigrant and Employee Rights Section 受理投诉的情形。
conventions.applies_when: US onboarding, after an offer is accepted and before or around the first day.
conventions.source_detail: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division — "IER's Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)", https://www.justice.gov/crt/iers-frequently-asked-questions-faqs, retrieved 2026-08-09. Verbatim: "The Department of Homeland Security has designated several combinations of acceptable documents from which workers can choose to prove their identity and permission to work... A worker is allowed to produce either List A documentation (establishing both identity and permission to work), or a combination of documentation from List B (establishing identity) and List C (establishing permission to work). Employers can't specify which documents they" [require]; "during both initial verification and reverification, a worker may choose which documentation to present from the List of Acceptable Documents"; and "Employers of any size cannot engage in unfair documentary practices related to verifying employees' employment eligibility during the I-9 and E-Verify processes. Specifically, employers are not allowed to, on the basis of citizenship, immigration status, or national origin, request more or different documents than are required to verify employment eligibility and identity, reject reasonably genuine-looking documents, or specify certain documents over others."
conventions.why: Onboarding paperwork feels like an administrative formality with no room to push back, and no posting or offer letter explains that the choice belongs to the worker. Candidates comply with a narrowed document demand and never learn it was improper.

conventions.text_en: The UK publishes a register of organisations licensed to sponsor workers on the Worker and Temporary Worker routes, and it lists the category of workers each organisation is licensed for and its sponsorship rating. A UK advert that is silent about visas tells you nothing; the register tells you whether the employer is set up to sponsor at all, and for what. The Skilled Worker route then needs an employer approved by the Home Office, a certificate of sponsorship from that employer, a job on the list of eligible occupations, and a salary floor that varies with the type of work and the date of the certificate — look the floor up on gov.uk rather than assuming a single figure, and note that a confirmed job offer must exist before the visa application is made. Consult the register before you spend effort on an application.
conventions.text_zh: 英国公开发布一份「已获许可的担保机构名录」，涵盖 Worker 与 Temporary Worker 路线，并载明每家机构被许可担保的工种类别及其担保评级。英国招聘启事对签证只字不提，并不代表任何信息；名录才能告诉你这家雇主是否具备担保资格、能担保什么类别。Skilled Worker 路线还要求：雇主经内政部批准、由该雇主签发担保证明（CoS）、职位在合格职业清单内，并达到薪资下限——而该下限随工作类型和 CoS 签发日期变动，请到 gov.uk 上查当期数值，不要假定是某个固定金额；另外，必须先有确定的工作邀约，才能提交签证申请。投出申请、投入精力之前，先查这份名录。
conventions.applies_when: Applying to any UK employer where sponsorship may eventually be needed.
conventions.source_detail: UK Visas and Immigration — "Register of licensed sponsors: workers", https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/register-of-licensed-sponsors-workers, retrieved 2026-08-09 (page shows Published 13 November 2013, Last updated 7 August 2026). Verbatim: "List of organisations licensed to sponsor workers on the Worker and Temporary Worker immigration routes." and "This document lists Worker and Temporary Worker sponsors. It includes information about the category of workers they're licensed to sponsor and their sponsorship rating." GOV.UK — "Skilled Worker visa: Overview", https://www.gov.uk/skilled-worker-visa, retrieved 2026-08-09. Verbatim: "To qualify for a Skilled Worker visa, you must: work for a UK employer that's been approved by the Home Office; have a 'certificate of sponsorship' (CoS) from your employer...; do a job that's on the list of eligible occupations; be paid a minimum salary - how much depends on the type of work you do and the date you got your CoS" and "You must have a confirmed job offer before you apply for your visa."
conventions.why: UK adverts frequently say nothing about sponsorship either way, so candidates cannot distinguish an employer that has never held a licence from one that simply did not mention it. The distinguishing fact is published by the government, not by the employer, and candidates do not know to look for it.

conventions.text_en: Every UK employer must check that a person is allowed to work for them before employing them, and can face a civil penalty for employing someone without a correct check — so being asked for right-to-work evidence is routine process applied to everyone the employer hires, not suspicion aimed at you, and gov.uk instructs employers that the process must not be used to discriminate. The check sits before the first day, not after it, so have your evidence ready by offer stage. Where an online check is used the candidate generates a share code themselves, but the choice of evidence is the candidate's: gov.uk states plainly that an employer cannot reject your application because you gave them an eligible immigration document instead of a share code.
conventions.text_zh: 英国的每一位雇主在正式雇用某人之前，都必须核查此人是否被允许为其工作；未做正确核查即雇用无权工作者，雇主可能面临民事罚款。因此被要求提供工作权利证明，是雇主对所有录用者一视同仁执行的常规流程，并非针对你的怀疑；gov.uk 也明确要求雇主不得借此实施歧视。这项核查发生在入职第一天之前，而不是之后，所以在收到 offer 阶段就应把材料准备好。若采用线上核查，分享码（share code）由候选人自己生成；但选择用哪种证明是候选人的权利：gov.uk 明确写明，雇主不能因为你提供的是合格的移民证件而非分享码，就拒绝你的申请。
conventions.applies_when: Any UK hiring process, from offer stage through to the day before you start.
conventions.source_detail: GOV.UK — "Checking a job applicant's right to work", https://www.gov.uk/check-job-applicant-right-to-work, retrieved 2026-08-09. Verbatim: "You must check that a job applicant is allowed to work for you in the UK before you employ them."; "You could face a civil penalty if you employ an illegal worker and have not carried out a correct right to work check."; "You must not discriminate against anyone because of where they're from." GOV.UK — "Prove your right to work to an employer: Overview", https://www.gov.uk/prove-right-to-work, retrieved 2026-08-09. Verbatim: "You'll need to prove your right to work in the UK to your employer before you start working for them." and "You can choose which option you use. Your employer cannot reject your application because you gave them an eligible immigration document instead of a share code, for example."
conventions.why: The advert says nothing about it, so the request arrives unannounced and reads as targeted scrutiny. Candidates also assume the employer dictates the format of proof and comply with whatever is demanded, not knowing the choice is theirs and the timing is fixed by law.

conventions.text_en: UK Civil Service recruitment runs on Success Profiles, assembled from behaviours, strengths, ability, experience and technical elements. Not all elements apply to a given role: the recruiting manager picks a selection of behaviours best suited to the job, the behaviours are defined separately for each grade level, and the job description names which ones will be assessed and by which method. The application typically asks for written examples against those named behaviours, and gov.uk itself recommends the STAR method so each example sets the scene, shows what you did and how, and gives the outcome. A general letter about why the organisation appeals to you scores nothing, because each named behaviour is marked on its own evidence. Adjustments to the assessment process can be requested from the recruiting manager.
conventions.text_zh: 英国公务员招聘采用 Success Profiles 框架，由 behaviours（行为）、strengths（优势）、ability（能力潜质）、experience（经验）、technical（专业技术）几个要素组合而成。并非每个职位都用到全部要素：招聘经理会挑选最契合该职位的若干项行为，且各项行为在不同职级上有各自的定义，职位说明书会写明本次考核哪几项、以何种方式考核。申请环节通常要求针对这些被点名的行为逐项撰写实例，gov.uk 本身就推荐使用 STAR 方法——交代背景、说明你做了什么和怎么做的、给出结果。泛泛地写一封「为什么想加入贵机构」的求职信得不到分数，因为每一项被点名的行为都按其自身证据单独评分。如需对考核流程作出调整，可以向招聘经理提出。
conventions.applies_when: Applying to any UK Civil Service role, or to a UK public body that states it recruits using Success Profiles.
conventions.source_detail: Cabinet Office — "Success Profiles", https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/success-profiles, retrieved 2026-08-09. Verbatim: "A Success Profile is made up of 5 elements: behaviours...; strengths...; ability...; experience...; technical..." and "Not all of the elements are relevant to every role." Cabinet Office — "Success Profiles: Civil Service behaviours", https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/success-profiles/success-profiles-civil-service-behaviours, updated 29 January 2025, retrieved 2026-08-09. Verbatim: "Civil Service Behaviours are specific to the grade level of the job role."; "recruiting managers will choose a selection of behaviours which are best suited to the specific job role. You will not be asked to demonstrate all Civil Service Behaviours for one role."; "application form requiring written examples" (listed among assessment methods); "In your own examples, consider using the STAR method which allows you to set the scene, show what and how you did and the overall outcome."; "If you need any reasonable adjustments to our recruitment process please let the recruiting manager know." The named behaviours on that page are: Seeing the big picture; Changing and improving; Making effective decisions; Leadership; Communicating and influencing; Working together; Developing self and others; Managing a quality service; Delivering at pace.
conventions.why: The advert names the behaviours but does not explain that they are separately scored, grade-calibrated units of assessment rather than themes to weave into prose. Candidates from markets where a cover letter is a persuasive essay write one, and score zero on criteria they never addressed head-on.

conventions.text_en: NHS shortlisting is scored against the person specification attached to the advert, which splits requirements into essential criteria — the qualifications, experience, skills or knowledge you must have to apply — and desirable criteria, which are used to separate applicants when many meet the essentials. NHS Jobs guidance is explicit that the applicants who closely match the person specification are the ones shortlisted, that you should never submit the same application twice but adapt it to the specification of that particular post, and that the supporting information is where you demonstrate how you meet it. The personal information and monitoring sections are not used for shortlisting. Evidence is entered criterion by criterion, and the official guide instructs applicants not to include personal information that could identify them, such as their name or contact details, in those boxes — so a signed narrative letter is the wrong artifact. Write to the specification, in its order, criterion by criterion.
conventions.text_zh: 英国 NHS 的初筛是对照招聘启事所附的「人员规格」（person specification）逐条打分的：该规格把要求分为 essential（必备）criteria——即申请所必须具备的学历、经验、技能或知识——以及 desirable（加分）criteria，后者用于在大量申请者都满足必备条件时进行区分。NHS Jobs 的官方指引明确写着：与人员规格高度吻合的申请者才会被列入面试短名单；绝不要重复提交同一份申请，而要针对该职位的人员规格逐次调整；supporting information（佐证信息）栏就是你证明自己符合各条要求的地方。personal information 与 monitoring information 两栏不用于初筛。佐证是按条目分框填写的，官方指南要求申请人不要在这些框内填入可用于识别本人身份的个人信息，例如姓名或联系方式——因此一封署名的叙述式求职信是错误的形式。请按人员规格的顺序，逐条对应地撰写。
conventions.applies_when: Applying to any NHS role through NHS Jobs, in any profession.
conventions.source_detail: NHS Jobs — "Making successful applications", https://www.jobs.nhs.uk/candidate/search/advice/making-successful-applications, retrieved 2026-08-09. Verbatim: "All employers will be judging how well your application matches the 'person specification' for the position you are applying for. The applicants who closely match the person specification will be the ones that are shortlisted for interview."; "Never submit the same application form twice. Always adapt it to show how you meet the person specification of the particular post you are applying for."; "The 'personal information' and 'monitoring information' sections will not be used for shortlisting, but will be kept for administrative purposes only." NHS Business Services Authority — "Applicant - What is the difference between essential and desirable criteria?", https://faq.nhsbsa.nhs.uk/knowledgebase/article/KA-25715/en-us, retrieved 2026-08-09. Verbatim: "Essential criteria are the qualifications, experience, skills or knowledge you must have to apply for a role." and "Desirable criteria are skills and experience that an employer would prefer. This may be used to decide who to invite to interview if they have a high volume of applications." NHSBSA — "How to apply for a job in NHS Jobs user guide – Add your supporting evidence", https://www.nhsbsa.nhs.uk/sites/default/files/2022-05/How%20to%20apply%20for%20a%20job%20in%20NHS%20Jobs%20-%20Add%20your%20supporting%20evidence.pdf, retrieved 2026-08-09. Verbatim: "Important: Do not include personal information that could be used to identify you such as your name or contact details." and "'Qualifications' and 'Experience' are mandatory essential criteria."
conventions.why: The advert publishes the person specification but does not say it is the scoring sheet, nor that the supporting section is graded criterion by criterion, nor that those boxes are meant to be anonymous. Candidates treat the specification as a wish list and write a flowing personal letter, which cannot be scored against criteria it never names.

entry.interview_shape:
UK CIVIL SERVICE — SOURCED. Cabinet Office lists the assessment methods used against Success Profile behaviours, and says the job description tells you which will apply: "Behaviours can be assessed in a number of ways and at various stages of the recruitment process, including: application form requiring written examples; Civil Service judgement test; personality test; interview; assessment centre; job related simulations such as: presentation; in-tray exercise; written analysis/exercise; group exercise/discussion; role-play; oral briefing." It also says "you may be asked to give examples of when you have demonstrated a particular behaviour" and, alternatively, "you may be asked how you would behave in a given situation. For example by using Situational Judgement Tests or through situational interview questions," and that "Your behaviours may be assessed alongside other elements of the Success Profile." Adjustments can be requested from the recruiting manager. What each round tests is therefore stated in the advert itself, per behaviour — which is unusual and worth exploiting. Source: gov.uk, "Success Profiles: Civil Service behaviours" (updated 29 January 2025), https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/success-profiles/success-profiles-civil-service-behaviours, retrieved 2026-08-09.

UK NHS — PARTLY SOURCED. The sequence begins with a paper sift scored against the person specification, and interview follows selection at that sift: "The applicants who closely match the person specification will be the ones that are shortlisted for interview," with desirable criteria used "to decide who to invite to interview if they have a high volume of applications." What happens inside the NHS interview itself (panel composition, values-based questions, clinical/practical stations) I COULD NOT SOURCE and is not claimed here. Sources: NHS Jobs, "Making successful applications," https://www.jobs.nhs.uk/candidate/search/advice/making-successful-applications; NHSBSA, "Applicant - What is the difference between essential and desirable criteria?", https://faq.nhsbsa.nhs.uk/knowledgebase/article/KA-25715/en-us. Both retrieved 2026-08-09.

US PRIVATE SECTOR — UNVERIFIED. The loop described in the brief (recruiter screen, then a mix of behavioural interviews, system-design rounds and a take-home exercise, then an onsite or virtual panel) is the widely repeated account of US technology hiring, but I found NO official or statutory source for it, and no source I was willing to cite for how the rounds are weighted or how often take-homes appear. It is recorded here as an unverified working assumption and MUST BE REVIEWED BY A PERSON before it ships. Do not attach any figure to it.

US PROCESS STAGES THAT ARE SOURCED. Two points in a US process are governed by rule rather than custom and can be relied on. Before or during application, an employer may ask whether you have the legal right to work in the US and whether you will need sponsorship (DOJ IER FAQ, https://www.justice.gov/crt/iers-frequently-asked-questions-faqs, retrieved 2026-08-09). After hire, Form I-9 verification occurs and the worker chooses the documents (same source). Neither is an interview round, but both are stages candidates fail to plan for.

US FEDERAL / USAJOBS — COULD NOT SOURCE. I attempted to retrieve USAJOBS help pages on federal résumé content and agency review; the site is a JavaScript application that returned no readable text by direct fetch and timed out on the rendering fetch. Nothing about the US federal hiring sequence is claimed here.

CROSS-MARKET DIFFERENCE THAT BURNS PEOPLE. UK public-sector processes publish, in the advert, the exact named criteria each stage will score, and expect written evidence structured to them (STAR is recommended by gov.uk itself). US processes generally do not publish their rubric. A candidate who brings the UK habit of writing tightly to published criteria into a US loop over-structures and under-sells; a candidate who brings a US narrative-and-rapport style into a UK Civil Service or NHS sift leaves named criteria unevidenced and is filtered before any human conversation.

review:
# Adversarial review — market `us_uk`

**Verification method:** every `source_kind: published` URL was fetched on 2026-08-09 (WebFetch, or curl where the host 403s WebFetch). Raw text saved under `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-donghanglyu/d1ca171b-6798-42dc-9582-87e4635be401/scratchpad/` (`ier.txt`, `t8.txt`, `ca.txt`, `cdle.txt`, `nhs.txt`, `nhsev.txt`, `csb.txt`, `prtw.html`). Constraint scan run mechanically via `scan.py`.

**All 13 cited URLs resolved HTTP 200 and every "Verbatim:" string was found in the fetched text — with two exceptions, both flagged below (a fabricated bracketed completion in #6, and one claim in #4 that is not on the page cited).**

## Cross-cutting constraint scan (mechanical, `scan.py`)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Percent sign | **None** in any `text_en`/`text_zh`. |
| Digits | Only in proper nouns: `H-1B` (#2), `Form I-983` (#3), `Form I-9` (#6). No digit is a quantity. |
| Written-out numbers | Only idiomatic `one`, `both`, `first`, `single` / `一`, `两`. No quantity claims. |
| Statistics | **None.** No entry attaches a figure to anything. |

If the lint is literal on `[0-9]`, #2/#3/#6 will fire on visa- and form-names. That is a lint problem, not an entry problem — do not let someone "fix" it by removing `H-1B` or `Form I-9`, which are the only strings that make those entries findable.

**Two places the no-digit rule has already cost real content** (lint-dodge, not compliance): #2's "the figure is set in the rule" hides `at least half of their work time` (8 CFR 214.2(h)(8)(iii)(F)(4), verified), and #5's "a size threshold set in the statute" hides `four or more employees` (NYSDOL, verified). A reader cannot act on either sentence as written. Fix by pointing at the source explicitly, not by leaving a blank.

---

## 1. `us-authorisation-and-sponsorship-are-separate-screens` — KEEP-WITH-EDIT

Source verified verbatim in `ier.txt`: *"Generally, an employer may ask job applicants if they have the legal right to work in the United States and if they will need sponsorship for an employment visa."* and *"An employer may restrict hiring to U.S. citizens only when a law, regulation, executive order, or government contract requires the employer to do so."*

**Overreach — the lead sentence outruns the source.** DOJ says an employer *may ask*. The entry says *"US application forms ask ... as separate questions"* — a claim about what forms actually do, and that the two are separate fields. Nothing in the source supports either. Second unsourced empirical claim: *"Whether the employer sponsors at all is normally a policy fixed before the role was ever advertised."* Third, in `why`: *"The posting almost never states the employer's sponsorship policy"* — an unmeasured frequency.

Replacement `text_en`:
> A US employer may ask whether you have the legal right to work in the United States, and separately whether you will need sponsorship for an employment visa — the Department of Justice confirms both questions are permitted. They are different questions, and where a form asks both, answer each on its own terms rather than collapsing them. The posting usually does not say whether the employer sponsors, so establish that before you invest further. One limit worth knowing: an employer may restrict hiring to US citizens only where a law, regulation, executive order or government contract requires it, and the Immigrant and Employee Rights Section takes complaints about citizenship-status discrimination where that is not the case.

Replacement `text_zh`:
> 美国雇主可以问「你是否有在美国合法工作的权利」，也可以另外再问「你是否需要签证担保」——美国司法部确认这两问都被允许。它们是不同的问题；申请表若两问都列，请分别如实回答，不要合并处理。招聘启事通常不会写明这家雇主是否提供担保，所以在继续投入之前先弄清楚。另有一条界限值得知道：只有在法律、法规、行政命令或政府合同要求时，雇主才可以把招聘限定为美国公民；不属于这些情形的「仅限美国公民」，司法部 Immigrant and Employee Rights Section 受理有关公民身份歧视的投诉。

Replacement `why`: *"The posting usually does not state the employer's sponsorship policy, and a rejection does not tell you which filter caught you."*

zh/en drift: none material. Protected trait: names citizenship status (protected under the INA) — unavoidable here, since the fact *is* a citizenship-discrimination rule; caller's call. Staleness: **low**.

## 2. `us-employer-class-decides-h1b-cap-exposure` — KEEP-WITH-EDIT

Source verified verbatim from the eCFR XML I fetched (`t8.txt`, offset ~320970), at **8 CFR 214.2(h)(8)(iii)(F)** — numbering in the entry is correct for the current text. Confirmed: the (F)(2) affiliation tests, and *"Work performed 'at' the qualifying institution may include work performed in the United States through telework, remote work, or other off-site work."* The registration claim is also supported: (h)(8)(iii)(A)(1) says registration is required *"before a petitioner can file an H-1B cap-subject petition"*.

**Three defects.**

(a) **Misstates the (F)(4) test.** Actual text: *"...will spend at least half of their work time performing job duties **at a qualifying institution**, organization, or entity **and** those job duties directly further an activity that supports or advances one of the fundamental purposes, missions, objectives, or functions..."* The entry drops the "at a qualifying institution" limb and keeps only the mission limb, which makes the test look broader than it is.

(b) **`why` contradicts the regulation the entry itself cites.** `why` says *"Cap-exempt status is a property of the employing organisation, not of the vacancy."* The same paragraph says *"USCIS will focus on the job duties to be performed, rather than where the duties are physically performed"* — and (F)(4) is a duties-and-time test. `text_en` gets this right; `why` gets it wrong.

(c) *"Postings never mention this"* — absolute, unsourced.

Replacement `text_en`:
> Some US employers sit in a statutory class exempt from the H-1B numerical cap: institutions of higher education, nonprofit entities related to or affiliated with them, nonprofit research organisations, and governmental research organisations. Postings rarely mention it, yet it changes what the employer can do and when, because the electronic registration requirement bites only on cap-subject petitions. The regulation also reaches past direct employment: someone employed elsewhere can still be cap-exempt if they spend at least the share of work time the rule specifies performing job duties at a qualifying institution and those duties directly further its higher-education, nonprofit-research or government-research mission — and work performed 'at' the institution may include telework, remote and other off-site work. Look the threshold up in the cited regulation before relying on it. What predicts the possibilities is the kind of organisation and the duties, not whether the advert says sponsorship is available.

Replacement `text_zh`:
> 有一类美国雇主在法规上不受 H-1B 名额上限限制：高等教育机构、与其存在关联或附属关系的非营利实体、非营利研究机构，以及政府研究机构。招聘启事很少提这一点，但它直接决定雇主能做什么、什么时候能做，因为电子登记（抽签）只对受名额限制的申请生效。法规还越过了「直接雇用」这一层：即使受雇于其他单位，只要本人把不低于法规所定份额的工作时间用于在合格机构从事职务，且这些职务直接服务于该机构的高等教育、非营利研究或政府研究使命，也可算作免名额；并且法规明确「在」该机构完成的工作可以包括远程与异地工作。具体门槛请按所引法规原文查证后再据以行动。所以真正能预测可行性的，是雇主属于哪类组织、职务内容为何，而不是启事上有没有写「提供签证担保」。

Replacement `why`: *"Cap exemption turns on the character of the employing organisation and on the duties performed, neither of which the advert describes. Candidates screen adverts for 'sponsorship available' and skip whole categories of employer for whom the annual cap is not the binding constraint."*

zh/en drift: none. Staleness: **medium-high** — this paragraph was renumbered in the recent H-1B modernization rulemaking (older secondary sources still cite `(h)(8)(ii)(F)`), and my citation is pinned to the eCFR `2026-08-01` snapshot. Re-verify the subparagraph letters annually.

## 3. `us-stem-opt-is-an-employer-side-requirement` — KEEP-WITH-EDIT

Source verified verbatim at 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C)(5) and (C)(6) in `t8.txt`, including the E-Verify "good standing" sentence, the EIN sentence, and the Form I-983 reporting-agreement sentence. Claim and source match exactly.

**One overreach:** *"Adverts never disclose E-Verify enrolment"* — absolute and unsourced, and I would not bet on it being true. Change `never` → `rarely`. Same in zh (`从不披露` → `很少披露`).

Only that word needs changing in both languages. Everything else in this entry survived scrutiny intact — it is the cleanest of the three US regulatory entries.

*Note for the missing-items list:* I tried to verify a public E-Verify participating-employer lookup so the entry could tell the reader how to check. `https://www.e-verify.gov/about-e-verify/e-verify-data/employer-search` returned **HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and curl** on 2026-08-09. **I am therefore not asserting that such a search exists** — do not add it without a successful fetch.

zh/en drift: none. Staleness: **medium** (STEM OPT rules have been subject to litigation and rulemaking).

## 4. `at-will-versus-notice-period-changes-your-start-date` — KEEP-WITH-EDIT (weakest entry; DROP is defensible)

California DIR PDF verified verbatim, including the footer `Termination of Employment (Rev. 1/2011)`: *"Within the State of California, employment may be terminated at the will of either party... Unless the parties have previously agreed to the contrary, there is no notice required to be given by either party."*

**(a) A claim that is not on the page cited.** `text_en` says *"your contract can require longer"*. The cited gov.uk page (`/handing-in-your-notice/giving-notice`, fetched in full) contains only: *"You must give at least a week's notice if you've been in your job for more than a month."*, *"Your contract will tell you whether you need to give notice in writing - otherwise you can do it verbally."*, and the breach sentence. I also fetched the sibling page `/handing-in-your-notice/your-employment-contract`, which says only *"If you want to leave your job, check your employment contract to find out your employer's policy on handing in notice."* **Neither page states that a contract can require longer notice.** Either source it separately or cut the clause.

**(b) Silently truncated "verbatim".** `source_detail` quotes *"You may be in breach of your contract if you do not give enough notice."* The actual sentence continues: *"...or give notice verbally when it should be given in writing."* Restore the full sentence or mark the ellipsis.

**(c) National claim, single-state source.** `text_en` opens *"US employment is at-will by default"* with no scoping, sourced to one state's labour agency. The `unverified` section is honest about this, but the rendered row is not — and the reader sees no source text.

**(d) Unsourced employer-behaviour claims:** *"US employers commonly expect a near-term start date and read a long notice period as a scheduling problem"* and *"the at-will wording in a US offer letter is standard boilerplate rather than a warning sign."* Nothing supports either.

**(e) `why` overstates:** *"promises a start date they cannot legally deliver."* Under the cited page, giving short notice risks **breach of contract**, not legal impossibility — and the statutory floor is short. Fix.

Replacement `text_en`:
> US employment is at-will in the ordinary case — California's labour standards agency states the doctrine plainly: either party may end the relationship at any time and, unless they agreed otherwise, neither owes the other notice. At-will is state law rather than a federal statute, so it is the default rather than a universal rule, and the customary short resignation notice is a norm, not an entitlement. The UK works the other way: gov.uk tells employees they must give at least a week's notice once they have been in the job beyond a short qualifying period, and warns that you may be in breach of your contract if you do not give enough notice or give it verbally when it should be in writing — so check your own contract, which may set the notice you owe. A UK start date is therefore negotiated around a notice period as a matter of course. If you are applying into both markets, state your availability against the right default in each.

Replacement `text_zh`:
> 美国的雇佣在通常情况下是「随意雇佣」（at-will）——加州劳工标准执行部门的官方表述是：任何一方都可以随时结束雇佣关系，除非双方另有约定，互不负提前通知义务。at-will 属于各州法而非联邦成文法，因此它是默认规则、不是放之全国皆准的铁律；惯例上的短期离职通知是习惯，不是法定权利。英国方向相反：gov.uk 告诉雇员，在职超过一段较短的资格期后，至少须提前一周通知，并提醒通知不足、或本应书面却口头通知，都可能构成违约——所以要查自己的合同，看它约定了多少通知期。因此英国的到岗日期天然是围绕通知期谈的。若同时投这两个市场，请按各自的默认规则分别声明你的可到岗时间。

If the table's rule is "no entry may state a national practice from a single-state source", then **DROP the US half and keep a UK-notice-only entry** — the UK half is fully sourced.

zh/en drift: none material (both carried the same defects). Staleness: **medium** on the UK side; the entry's own `unverified` item 6 correctly flags that UK employment law is in flux.

## 5. `us-pay-range-in-a-posting-is-jurisdictional-not-cultural` — KEEP-WITH-EDIT

Both sources verified verbatim. Colorado (`cdle.txt`): *"Part 2, referred to by the Division as 'Pay Transparency,' requires transparency in pay and job opportunities.
